title: Instrumental: Exceptions & Edge Cases
titleRussian: Творительный падеж: исключения и особые случаи
description: The forms that fall outside the regular -ом / -ой / -ью pattern: the мать / дочь stem extension drilled in production, instrumental of plural-only nouns (часами, ножницами, сутками, деньгами), frozen adverbial instrumentals beyond time-of-day (бегом, шагом, рядом, пешком), and a brief look at the instrumental of small numerals (двумя, тремя, четырьмя).
descriptionRussian: Формы, выпадающие из обычной модели -ом / -ой / -ью: расширение основы у слов мать и дочь с акцентом на продукцию, творительный падеж существительных pluralia tantum (часами, ножницами, сутками, деньгами), застывшие наречные творительные за пределами времени суток (бегом, шагом, рядом, пешком) и краткий обзор творительного у малых числительных (двумя, тремя, четырьмя).
intro: The usual suspects one more time: мать and дочь with their extra syllable, and the nouns that exist only in the plural. New here is a small set of bare instrumentals that have hardened into adverbs of manner, so that the word for 'step' now means 'at walking pace'. Those you learn as vocabulary rather than as grammar.
rules: Мать and дочь take a stem extension in every case except the nominative-accusative singular. In the instrumental, the long stem мат-ер- / доч-ер- gets the -ью ending directly: матерью, дочерью. Not матью or дочью.

Plurale-tantum nouns (часы, ножницы, сутки, деньги, очки, ворота) have no singular. Their instrumental is the regular instrumental plural ending -ами / -ями: часами, ножницами, сутками, деньгами, очками, воротами.

Certain bare instrumental forms have hardened into adverbs of manner: бегом (hurriedly), шагом (at walking pace), рядом (nearby), пешком (on foot), кругом (all around), верхом (on horseback), голосом / шёпотом (out loud / in a whisper). They are used without a preposition and no longer feel like nouns.

Small-number phrases take their own instrumental: с двумя, с тремя, с четырьмя, plus the matching instrumental plural of the noun: с двумя друзьями, с тремя сёстрами, с четырьмя ребятами. (The full system of declining numerals belongs to b1-numerals-mastery; recognise these forms here.)
examples: Я горжусь матерью. (I am proud of my mother.) Stem extension мат-ер- + -ью; not матью.
Маша гуляет с дочерью. (Masha is walking with her daughter.) Stem extension доч-ер- + -ью; not дочью.
Лена работала сутками. (Lena worked round the clock, for days on end.) Plurale tantum сутки → сутками, adverbial.
Антон ждал нас часами. (Anton waited for us for hours on end.) Plurale tantum часы → часами, adverbial.
Не размахивай ножницами! (Don't wave the scissors around!) Plurale tantum ножницы → ножницами; махать + instrumental.
Они расплатились деньгами, а не картой. (They paid with cash, not a card.) Plurale tantum деньги → деньгами; instrumental of means.
Лена бегом побежала домой. (Lena ran home hurriedly.) Frozen adverbial бегом from бег.
Дети шагом перешли дорогу. (The children crossed the road at a walking pace.) Frozen adverbial шагом from шаг.
Я живу рядом со школой. (I live next to the school.) Frozen adverbial рядом from ряд.
Мы пришли на стадион пешком. (We came to the stadium on foot.) Frozen adverbial пешком.
Я разговаривал с двумя друзьями. (I spoke with two friends.) Small-number instrumental: двумя + instrumental plural друзьями.
Антон работает с тремя коллегами. (Anton works with three colleagues.) тремя + instrumental plural коллегами.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is proud of his mother.
items.hint: Гордиться + instrumental. Мать takes a stem extension before its endings.
items.explanation: Мать has a long stem мат-ер- in every case except the nominative-accusative singular. The instrumental adds -ью directly to that long stem: матерью.

items.promptEnglish: Masha often goes for a walk with her daughter.
items.hint: Дочь is the other word with the stem extension. С + instrumental.
items.explanation: Дочь is the second of the two kinship nouns with the long stem (доч-ер-). С meaning 'together with' takes the instrumental, and the instrumental of дочь is дочерью.

items.promptEnglish: Lena worked on this project for days on end.
items.hint: Сутки is a plurale-tantum noun. The adverbial 'for days on end' is the instrumental plural.
items.explanation: Сутки ('a full 24-hour day') exists only in the plural; there is no singular. The instrumental plural is regular: сутками. Used adverbially, it means 'for days on end / round the clock.' Compare часами (for hours on end) from часы.

items.promptEnglish: We walked to the park on foot.
items.hint: 'On foot' is a frozen bare-instrumental adverb.
items.explanation: Пешком is one of the frozen instrumental adverbials of manner. It is used without any preposition and is no longer felt as a noun. The bare instrumental of бег → бегом ('hurriedly') and шаг → шагом ('at walking pace') work the same way.

items.promptEnglish: Anton waited for us for hours on end in the rain.
items.hint: The plural noun часы here is being used adverbially: 'for hours on end.'
items.explanation: Часы (the plural noun 'clock / watch / hours-on-end') takes the regular instrumental plural часами. Used adverbially, часами means 'for hours on end.'

items.promptEnglish: The wind slammed the door loudly.
items.hint: Дверь is a third-declension -ь noun. The instrumental adds -ью directly, with no stem extension.
items.explanation: Дверь is a regular third-declension feminine noun: the instrumental adds -ью straight onto the stem, дверью, with none of the stem extension that мать and дочь require. Compare ночь → ночью.

blanks: Маша расплатилась _____, а не картой. (Masha paid with cash, not a card.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Деньги ('money') exists only in the plural. The instrumental of means uses the regular instrumental plural ending -ами: деньгами.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha is proud of her mother.
minimalPairs.explanation: Мать takes the long stem мат-ер- in every case except the nominative-accusative singular. The instrumental is матерью, not матью. Матью looks like a naive regularisation (compare ночь → ночью) but the stem extension wins.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Lena crossed the road at a walking pace.
minimalPairs.explanation: Шагом is the frozen instrumental adverb of manner from шаг ('a step / pace'). It means 'at a walking pace,' contrasted with бегом ('at a run'). The bare nominative шаг would not fit an adverbial slot.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton sprinkled salt on his soup.
errorCorrection.explanation: Соль is a 3rd-declension feminine (soft -ь), so its instrumental adds -ью: солью. Солю drops the soft sign and applies a regular ending; it is not a valid form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The children walk beside the horse.
errorCorrection.explanation: Лошадь is a 3rd-declension feminine, so the instrumental after с is лошадью. Лошадю applies a bare -ю without the soft-sign cluster and is not a valid form.

errorCorrection.sentence: Летом дети играют во дворе днями.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In summer the children play in the yard for days on end.
errorCorrection.explanation: The adverbial time-instrumental plural means 'for days on end': днями, parallel to часами and сутками. The form needed is the instrumental plural -ами/-ями. Дням is the dative plural, not the instrumental.

errorCorrection.sentence: В магазине Маша расплатилась деньги, а не картой.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: At the store Masha paid with cash, not a card.
errorCorrection.explanation: Деньги ('money') exists only in the plural, and the instrumental of means uses the regular instrumental-plural ending -ами: деньгами. The bare деньги is the nominative, which cannot mark the means of payment. The parallel with картой (also instrumental, 'by card') confirms the case: both means take the instrumental, so деньгами.

Бегом is a frozen instrumental adverb of manner meaning 'at a run, hurriedly', built from бег ('a run'). It stands alone without any preposition. Бегу is the dative, which never works as a manner adverb. The same frozen pattern gives шагом ('at a walking pace') and пешком ('on foot').

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena carefully cuts the paper with scissors.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ножницы ('scissors') exists only in the plural, and the instrument of an action takes the instrumental: the regular instrumental-plural ending -ами gives ножницами. The bare ножницы is the nominative, which cannot mark the tool. 'Cut with scissors' = резать ножницами.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each instrumental form by which exception class it belongs to.

patternRecognition.promptEnglish: Masha is proud of her mother.
patternRecognition.explanation: Гордиться takes the instrumental. Мать has the long stem мат-ер-: матерью.

patternRecognition.promptEnglish: Anton waited for us for hours on end.
patternRecognition.explanation: The adverbial 'for hours on end' uses the instrumental plural of the plural-only noun часы: часами.

patternRecognition.promptEnglish: We came to the park on foot.
patternRecognition.explanation: Пешком is the frozen instrumental adverb of manner; it stands without a preposition. The other options are adjective forms and would not fit an adverbial slot.

patternRecognition.promptEnglish: Grandma reads the newspaper using her glasses.
patternRecognition.explanation: Очки ('glasses') is a plural-only noun, and пользоваться takes the instrumental, so the regular instrumental plural очками is needed.

reviewVocab.definition: instrumental of мать / дочь. Both take a stem extension (мат-ер-, доч-ер-) before the -ью ending. Not матью or дочью.
часы, ножницы, сутки, деньги, очки, ворота: nouns that exist only in the plural. The instrumental is the regular instrumental plural ending -ами / -ями: часами, ножницами, сутками, деньгами.
reviewVocab.example: Лена работала сутками. / Я ждал часами. / Они расплатились деньгами.

reviewVocab.definition: бегом (hurriedly), шагом (at walking pace), рядом (nearby), пешком (on foot), кругом (all around), верхом (on horseback): bare instrumental forms used without a preposition as adverbs of manner.
reviewVocab.example: Лена бегом побежала домой. / Мы пришли пешком. / Я живу рядом.

reviewVocab.definition: instrumental of the small numerals 2 / 3 / 4, used in phrases like 'with two friends.' The full numeral declension system belongs to b1-numerals-mastery; here you only need to recognise these forms.
reviewVocab.example: С двумя друзьями, с тремя сёстрами, с четырьмя ребятами.
